title: Lumen Copilot WebSocket envelope
description: Transport framing for ALL WebSocket traffic (ADR-0003 §8, contracts/AGENTS.md). Every message is an envelope discriminated by `type`. Concrete product event payloads are slotted into `data` per `type`. Stream lifecycle: start -> (delta | event)* -> done | error, with exactly one terminal (done|error). The chat feature's payloads (issue #37, CC-6 #24 / CC-11 #26) are defined under $defs and mapped by x-chatStream.

streamId.description: Correlates all messages of one logical stream (the chat send returns this as stream_id).

seq.description: Monotonically increasing per streamId; defines ordering.

data.description: Stream-open metadata; shape defined per feature (chat: ChatStartData).
Incremental output (e.g. a token chunk). Payload shape defined per feature (chat: ChatTokenDelta).

name.description: Structured side-band event name. Chat vocabulary: citation, tool_call, tool_result, code_output, code_result (the last two carry sandbox code-run output/outcome, ADR-0013 #229).

data.description: Terminal success summary; shape defined per feature (chat: ChatDoneData).

problem.description: Same problem model as the REST error shape (openapi.yaml #/components/schemas/Problem).

messageId.description: Id the in-progress assistant message will be persisted under.

ChatTokenDelta.description: `delta.data` — one streamed chunk of the assistant answer.

ChatCitation.description: `event.data` for name=citation. Mirrors openapi Citation (spec 0004 INV-3): a permitted passage the answer cites. The UI renders it as a clickable reference resolving to the document + span.

ChatToolCall.description: `event.data` for name=tool_call — the agent invoked a governed tool (CC-6 #24 / CC-7 #207). Surfaced so the UI can show 'searching…'. Every call is permission-filtered + allow-list-checked + audited via the tool registry (INV-2/INV-6).

tool.description: The registered tool name (CC-7 #207 — the tool set is open-ended). MVP retrieval tools: search_text = hybrid semantic+lexical passage search; search_documents = by filename/metadata; list_documents = enumerate the documents the user can access (no query); get_document = fetch a permitted document's text.

ChatToolResult.description: `event.data` for name=tool_result — outcome of a tool_call (CC-7 #207). A denied (off-allow-list / unapproved) or failing tool is reported as ok=false with a typed error, never a crashed stream.

tool.description: The registered tool name (CC-7 #207 — the tool set is open-ended).

ok.description: Whether the tool succeeded. Absent ⇒ treat as ok (back-compat). Additive (CC-7 #207).

error.description: Typed error code when ok=false (e.g. tool_not_permitted, approval_denied, tool_error, tool_timeout). Additive (CC-7 #207).

ChatDoneData.description: `done.data` — terminal success summary for a chat answer.

cachedPromptTokens.description: Prompt tokens served from the provider's prompt cache this answer (#409, ADR-0016 §2.6). Additive; 0 when the provider reports no cache detail.

cacheWriteTokens.description: Prompt tokens written INTO the provider's prompt cache this answer (Anthropic-style cache creation). Additive; 0 when unreported.

CodeOutput.description: `event.data` for name=code_output — one streamed chunk of a sandbox code run's output (ADR-0013 §4, epic #200). Emitted within the chat answer stream while the agent's `run_python` tool (CC-A #207) executes: it lets the inspector UI (#232) show stdout/stderr live (E6-5 debuggable runs). `stream` says whether the chunk is stdout or stderr; multiple code_output events per `runId` arrive in `seq` order. Non-terminal — the run's outcome arrives as a single code_result. Chunks are output-size-capped (§2/G7); a truncating run still terminates with code_result.

runId.description: The code_runs.id this output belongs to (matches GET /code-runs/{codeRunId}).

callId.description: Correlates to the originating tool_call (ChatToolCall.callId) when the run was launched by a run_python tool call. Optional.

stream.description: Which output stream this chunk came from.

text.description: The chunk of captured output (may be truncated at the output-size cap, G7).

CodeResult.description: `event.data` for name=code_result — the terminal-ish outcome of a sandbox code run (ADR-0013 §4). Exactly one arrives per `runId` after its code_output chunks, carrying the run's final `status`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, and the ids of any emitted artifacts (`artifactIds`, collected via CC-B #208). This is a run-level terminal event, NOT the chat stream's terminal — the chat stream still ends with its own done|error. The full record (code, stdout/stderr, resource usage) is inspectable via GET /code-runs/{runId}.

runId.description: The code_runs.id this result finalizes (matches GET /code-runs/{codeRunId}).

callId.description: Correlates to the originating tool_call (ChatToolCall.callId) when applicable. Optional.

status.description: The run's terminal status (mirrors openapi CodeRunStatus, minus the non-terminal queued/running).

exitCode.description: Process exit code; null when killed/timeout/denied before producing one.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock execution time in milliseconds; null when the run never started (denied).

artifactIds.description: Ids of artifacts the run emitted (files collected + persisted via CC-B #208, tenant-scoped). Empty when the run produced none.

x-chatStream.description: Concrete payloads carried by a chat answer stream (issue #37). The transport envelope (root oneOf) is unchanged; these define what rides in `data` per `type`/`name`. When the agent runs code via the run_python tool (CC-A #207, ADR-0013 #229), the sandbox output rides this same stream as event:code_output / event:code_result — additive, non-terminal for the chat stream itself.
x-chatStream.lifecycle: start(ChatStartData) -> ( delta(ChatTokenDelta) | event:tool_call(ChatToolCall) | event:tool_result(ChatToolResult) | event:citation(ChatCitation) | event:code_output(CodeOutput) | event:code_result(CodeResult) )* -> done(ChatDoneData) | error(Problem)
x-chatStream.codeRunSubStream: A run_python tool_call opens a code-run sub-sequence on the SAME chat stream, correlated by runId (and the originating tool_call's callId): zero or more event:code_output(CodeOutput) chunks in seq order, terminated by exactly one event:code_result(CodeResult) per runId. code_result is a run-level terminal, NOT the chat stream's terminal — the chat stream still ends with its own done|error. The full, output-size-capped run record (code, stdout/stderr, resource_usage) is inspectable at GET /code-runs/{runId}, tenant/owner-scoped (cross-tenant runId -> 404).
x-chatStream.subscribe: After POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages returns { stream_id }, connect to GET /ws/chat/{stream_id}?access_token=<access JWT>. A browser WebSocket cannot set the Authorization header, so the access token rides the `access_token` query param. The stream is bound to its owner at send time; a missing/invalid token or a foreign/cross-tenant subscriber is denied identically (handshake rejected, no envelope emitted).
